How to look after a wool jumper

Wool is self-cleaning to a surprising degree. Airing a jumper overnight often does more good than a wash.

When it does need washing, use cold water and a wool detergent, and never wring it — press the water out between two towels instead.

Dry flat, away from direct heat, and fold rather than hang to keep the shoulders in shape.

Pilling happens where fibres rub. A wool comb lifts it off in a minute and the jumper will pill less over time.

Store folded with cedar in a breathable bag, and your jumper will last for years.

Moths prefer dark, undisturbed places and clothes that have been worn but not washed, so put jumpers away clean and take them out now and then over summer.

Small holes can be darned with matching yarn. A darning mushroom helps keep the tension even, and a visible contrasting darn has become a style of its own.

If a jumper shrinks, soak it in lukewarm water with a little hair conditioner, then gently stretch it back into shape and dry it flat.

Above all, wear it often. A well-loved wool jumper softens with age and outlasts almost anything else in the wardrobe.
